title: Candy

description.main: Candy (self-published, 2015) is the second of Aaron McElroy's three Sugar series books: wire-bound black and white nudes, old and new, laser-printed by the artist. 56 pages, 50 illustrations, 8 x 11 inches.
description.extended:
Candy is the middle book of Aaron McElroy's Sugar series, a self-published set of black and white nudes that he printed himself on a laser printer and bound with wire.

Issued in late 2015, a few months after Sweet, it brings older pictures together with new ones and treats the female figure as line and shape, with the flat blacks and broken tones of laser printing left in as part of the picture. McElroy printed the pink cover, set with the title alone in red script, on 215 gsm inkjet stock and the pages on 70 lb ivory paper. 56 pages with 50 illustrations at 8 x 11 inches. photo-eye lists an edition of 150. The artist's own site and the Independent Photo Book announced 120.

McElroy is a New York photographer and a founder of S_U_N, the cooperative that published Sweet and his larger colour book The Devil May Care (2014). The series closed with Sugar in 2016. The library holds all three volumes, along with Briney Breezes, his two-artist book with Charles Johnstone.
description.artist_bio: Aaron McElroy (b. 1978, Daytona) is a New York photographer and a founding member of S_U_N, the photographers' cooperative. Studied at the New England School of Photography. Books include The Devil May Care (S_U_N, 2014), Sweet (S_U_N, 2015), Reds (S_U_N) and Briney Breezes (with Charles Johnstone, 2015).

notes: Sugar Series, volume 2 of 3. Signed by McElroy. Edition: photo-eye says printed in an edition of 150; the artist's own site (archived Nov 2016), the Independent Photo Book (4 Dec 2015) and an AbeBooks dealer copy (Studio Bibliografico Marini) all say 120. Page count: photo-eye 56 pp.; artist's site and dealer 55. Specs (56 pp., 50 ills., 8x11 in, 215 gsm inkjet cover, 70 lb ivory contents) from photo-eye. Dashwood sold the three volumes as a set limited to 50, each signed; that figure is the set, not this volume. Cover file is a dealer photograph of a copy (AbeBooks, 1125x1500, cropped); photo-eye's flat product image (316x435) is the alternative.
